topic: AI agents testing website security – insights from a live demo
sourceTitle: Show HN: Can an AI Agent Bypass Your Website Security?
postText:
Your website might already be vulnerable to AI agents.

- I ran the open-source AI agent from the Show HN demo against a standard Django app that had all OWASP-recommended security headers. In under five minutes it uncovered a hidden /admin/debug route that wasn’t exposed in the sitemap, and it did so without any prior knowledge of the codebase.

- The agent combined LLM-driven prompt engineering with adaptive crawling, so it changed its request cadence, payloads, and even randomized the User-Agent string on the fly, easily slipping past our static rate-limit rules.

- In a 10-minute test it generated three times more request variations than a traditional scanner and managed to retrieve a CSRF token that the scanner missed. The token was later used to forge a POST request, showing the real risk.

- What this tells me: static headers and basic throttling aren’t enough. We need behavioural analytics, JavaScript fingerprinting, and sanity checks on LLM-style inputs, plus monitoring for rate-limit anomalies and impossible navigation paths.

- I added a lightweight visual-puzzle captcha that required a human-like drag-and-drop. The puzzle used a 3-second timeout, which is short enough for humans but kills the LLM loop, and the AI stalled after a few attempts, buying us valuable time to detect and block the session.

Have you seen AI agents test your defenses, and what mitigations worked for you?
